extracted.intended_audience: Prospective bidders, offshore wind developers, and other stakeholders (fishing industry, state/local agencies, Tribes, and public commenters) for the New York Bight lease sale
extracted.subtask_short: NY Bight offshore wind lease PSN
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed Sale Notice (PSN) describing areas, procedures, deadlines, qualification and auction rules, lease terms, and topics on which BOEM requests public comment for the Atlantic Wind Lease Sale 8 (ATLW-8) in the New York Bight. Useful for preparing comments, bidder qualification materials, and bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission deadline and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments are due by August 13, 2021. Submit comments electronically at regulations.gov (Docket No. BOEM-2021-0033) or by mail to BOEM's specified address. Comments must include the agency name (BOEM) and docket number (BOEM-2021-0033).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments received will be posted without change to regulations.gov, including any personal information. See section XX (Public Participation) and section XXI (Protection of Privileged or Confidential Information) for instructions on confidentiality. BOEM does not consider anonymous comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder legal, technical, and financial qualifications (30 CFR 585.106-.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities must establish legal, technical, and financial qualifications pursuant to 30 CFR 585.106 and 585.107 to be eligible to participate in the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective bidders who have not been qualified must submit qualification materials during the comment period (postmarked no later than Aug 13, 2021). BOEM will finalize qualification reviews prior to FSN publication and publish the final list of eligible bidders in the FSN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliated entities disclosure and affiliation rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidders must list on the Bidder's Financial Form (BFF) any other eligible bidders with whom they are affiliated. Affiliated eligible bidders are not permitted to compete against each other in the lease sale and must decide which eligible bidder will participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM considers entities affiliated if one has any right, title, or interest in the other (including control) or they are subsidiaries of the same parent. If affiliated bidders nonetheless participate, BOEM may disqualify some or all of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder's Financial Form (BFF) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bidder must submit a completed BFF to BOEM by the date listed in the FSN to participate in the auction; new BFFs required for this sale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BFF should be accompanied by a transmittal letter on company letterhead; BOEM prefers a company email; BFF must be executed by an authorized representative listed on the legal qualifications; self-certification must comply with 18 U.S.C. 1001. BOEM will consider the email sent date to OREP mailbox as official receipt. Digital signatures acceptable until further notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bid deposit amount and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each bidder must provide a bid deposit of $5,000,000. If FSN allows bidding on two leases, deposit would be $10,000,000 for two-lease bidding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bid deposits are due no later than the date listed in the FSN to participate in the mock auction and monetary auction. BOEM may consider extensions only if failure was due to events beyond bidder's control. Non-winners will receive returned deposits (with explanation) after auction; winners forfeit deposit if they fail to comply with post-auction obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of lease areas per bidder (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes to allow each qualified entity to bid for only one lease in any given round and ultimately acquire only one lease area; BOEM is seeking comment and has considered allowing up to two lease areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM solicits feedback on how this scheme may affect competition and electricity costs; commenters should consider number and size of lease areas when responding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction format — single-factor ascending-bid with two-stage assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sale proposed as a single-factor ascending-bid auction with two-stage winner determination (Stage 1: select combination of final-round live bids maximizing sum subject to constraints; Stage 2: consider bids from all rounds to assign remaining Lease Areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constraints include bidders must win all Lease Areas included in their final-round live bid, either live or intra-round bid (not both) may be selected, and Lease Areas cannot be assigned to multiple bids. Tie-breaking procedures move tied combinations to Stage 2 and then use stage-2 maximization or pseudorandom numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mock auction participation
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will hold a mock auction open only to qualified bidders who have met participation requirements (including bid deposit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final mock auction details will be provided in the FSN. Authentication tokens and login credentials will be tested during the mock auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder authentication and tokens
rubrics_metrics.description: Online auction requires two-factor authentication. Auction contractor will send authentication packages containing digital/hardware tokens and login credentials to authorized individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Up to three individuals may be authorized to bid per bidder. Tokens must be returned within three business days after the auction. BOEM may mail credentials directly to authorized bidders in certain circumstances. Auction access testing occurs during the mock auction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidder operational readiness and backup procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidders are responsible for ensuring working internet connection and backup procedures (redundant connections, multiple authorized bidders, alternate sites, 4G mobile data) in case of connectivity failure during the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders should test backup procedures during the mock auction; BOEM will not accept connectivity failures as an excuse unless covered by FSN provisions or extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auction messaging and schedule changes
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM and contractors will use the auction platform messaging service to notify bidders of schedule changes or other updates during the auction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If BOEM changes schedule during the auction, messaging feature will alert bidders and direct them to relevant pages. Bidders must monitor messages for updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional winners post-auction obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 business days of receiving lease copies, provisionally winning bidders must sign and return the lease copies, file required financial assurance (30 CFR 585.515-537), and pay by EFT the balance of the bonus bid (winning bid minus bid deposit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First year's rent is due 45-calendar days after receipt of lease copies. BOEM may extend the 10-business-day deadline for events beyond bidder's control. Failure to comply may result in forfeiture of bid deposit and BOEM offering the lease to next highest bidder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection or non-acceptance of bids
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM reserves the right to reject any and all bids that do not satisfy auction/FSN/regulatory requirements and statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may provide explanations for rejections; bidders can seek reconsideration per appeals procedures. BOEM may disqualify provisionally winning bidders found to have violated auction rules or engaged in detrimental conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-competitive review and behavior examples (43 U.S.C. 1337(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: After auction, DOJ (in consultation with FTC) has 30 days to review results for antitrust concerns. BOEM will decline to award leases if the Attorney General/FTC determine awarding would be inconsistent with antitrust laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of anti-competitive behavior include express/tacit agreements among bidders not to bid or to bid particular prices, agreements not to bid on certain Lease Areas, agreements not to bid against each other, or other agreements affecting final price. Compliance with BOEM procedures is not an absolute defense to antitrust violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of blocks/reservation of right to change lease areas
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM reserves the right to withdraw all or portions of the Lease Areas prior to executing leases with winning bidders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lease area boundaries may change (e.g., due to USCG or DoD concerns); bidders should be aware that lease areas are not final until lease execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease terms, conditions, and required attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed leases include Addenda A (Leased Area & Activities), B (Lease Term & Financial Schedule), C (Lease Specific Terms, Conditions, and Stipulations), D (Project Easement), E (Rent Schedule Post COP Approval), Appendix A to Addendum C (Incident Report: Protected Species Injury or Mortality), and Appendix B (Required Data Elements for Protected Species Observer Reports).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addenda A–C provide detailed lease terms and conditions; Addendum D completed at COP approval; Addendum E completed after COP approval. BOEM may require compliance with additional terms associated with SAP or COP approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required plans and timing (SAP and COP)
rubrics_metrics.description: If site assessment activities will be conducted, lessee must submit a Site Assessment Plan (SAP) within 12 months of lease issuance. A Construction and Operations Plan (COP) is required for development activities and will be reviewed for environmental, technical, and navigational concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may require additional mitigation measures during COP review, informed by site-specific navigational safety risk assessments and consultations (USCG, DoD, NMFS, USFWS, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential navigational safety restrictions (USCG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Portions of lease areas (e.g., Hudson North) may not be available for development due to USCG traffic lanes, safety fairways, and outcomes of Port Access Route Studies (PARS). BOEM may require mitigation or adjust lease boundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation measures could be required at COP stage; bidders should be aware that USCG ANPRM and PARS may result in additional east/west mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vessel transit corridors design and no-surface-occupancy overlaps
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM identified initial vessel transit corridors in Hudson South with proposed width of 2.44 nautical miles; where lease area overlaps transit corridors, no surface occupancy will be allowed within overlap areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM seeks comment on corridor attributes, orientation, and whether uniform turbine layouts could negate need for transit corridors. Bidders should consider transit corridors when planning layouts and operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Defense coordination and potential restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM coordinates with DoD; potential conflicts may lead to development restrictions (e.g., turbine height restrictions to less than 1,000 ft to avoid NEXRAD impacts), mitigation for air surveillance/radar impacts, or portions of lease areas being unavailable for development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM is refining DoD evaluations and will publish additional information in the FSN; bidders should note possible site-specific restrictions and mitigation conditions to be addressed at COP stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation and confidentiality of comments
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM does not consider anonymous comments. Comments must include name and address; submissions will be publicly available on regulations.gov unless the commenter identifies information that would constitute a clearly unwarranted invasion of privacy and explains possible harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request that BOEM withhold PII, identify and briefly describe possible harmful consequences. BOEM cannot guarantee nondisclosure because a court may order release. Information not labeled confidential may be released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of privileged or confidential information (FOIA Exemption 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will protect trade secrets and commercial or financial information that is privileged or confidential (5 U.S.C. 552(b)(4)), as required by FOIA and 30 CFR 585.113.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To protect confidentiality, clearly mark submissions 'Contains Privileged or Confidential Information' and consider submitting such information as a separate attachment. BOEM will not treat aggregate summaries of non-confidential information as confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to information regarding historic resources (54 U.S.C. 307103)
rubrics_metrics.description: After consultation with Secretary of the Interior, BOEM may withhold location, character, or ownership of historic resources if disclosure could cause invasion of privacy, risk harm, or impede traditional religious site use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribal entities and interested parties should designate information they wish withheld and provide reasons for confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulations/incentives for benefits to underserved communities
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM is considering lease stipulations or incentives (auction credits, rent/operating fee credits) to direct benefits to underserved communities (workforce training/development, contracting with minority- and women-owned businesses, environmental justice programs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulations could mandate or encourage use of instruments with reporting requirements; BOEM invites comment on appropriate mechanisms, evaluation metrics, valuation of requirements, and examples of measures that further OCS Lands Act purposes. Commenters should provide supporting studies and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for creating a domestic supply chain
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM is considering mechanisms such as lease stipulations, auction credits, or credits towards rent and operating fees to incentivize a durable domestic supply chain for offshore wind development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should describe how such measures would further development and provide references to studies supporting recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessee engagement and coordination with ocean users and Tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM proposes a lease stipulation requiring semi-annual progress reports summarizing engagement with ocean users potentially affected by lease activities (identify existing users; describe engagement; efforts to avoid/minimize/mitigate conflicts; planned next steps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stipulation would specifically require coordination with fishing industry and consideration of conflicts prior to proposing turbine layout in COP. BOEM seeks comments on contents and timing of such reports and on methods for coordinated engagement (frequency, format). Government-to-Government Tribal consultations remain BOEM responsibility and are not substituted by lessee meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed turbine layouts consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM asks whether prescribing uniform and aligned turbine layouts (especially in Hudson South) should be considered and whether such layouts would negate the need for established transit corridors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM seeks technical input on tradeoffs between uniform layouts and transit corridors; commenters should submit technical/scientific data supporting preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed rent calculation simplification
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM is seeking feedback on simplifying rent calculation for portions of lease area not yet authorized for commercial operations by dividing authorized area into 'generating' and 'non-generating' acreage and using non-generating acreage as basis for rental calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should provide analysis on preferred rental structure and impacts on lessees and government returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to comment on industry environmental protection standards
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM seeks comments on new industry standards (technology standards, vessel standards, etc.) for environmental protection across phases of development that BOEM should consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references and justification for recommended standards; BOEM may adopt or reference such standards in lease stipulations or COP/SAP conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines, milestones, and FSN timing
rubrics_metrics.description: PSN comment period is 60 days; BOEM will review comments, finalize qualifications, prepare and publish FSN in Federal Register (FSN published at least 30 days before lease sale). Auction occurs no sooner than 30 days after FSN publication (estimated ~45 days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified bidders must submit BFF and bid deposits by FSN-specified dates; winners must execute leases and pay first-year rent within specified timeframes. BOEM may extend deadlines for events beyond a bidder's control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and reconsideration procedures (30 CFR 585.225; 585.118(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM rejects a bid, it will provide a written statement of reasons and refund deposits; bidders can ask BOEM Director for reconsideration in writing within 15 business days of bid rejection under 30 CFR 585.118(c)(1). Appeals of final decisions described in 30 CFR 585.118(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow regulatory citations for formal appeal timelines and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-procurement debarment and suspension compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Lessee must comply with Department of the Interior's non-procurement debarment and suspension regulations at 2 CFR parts 180 and 1400 and must communicate this requirement to persons with whom the lessee does business relating to the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee should include this term in contracts and transactions related to the lease.
